hook.line: Sooner or later in Bogotá someone will say the building is being sold, or the bill is higher than you thought. Spanish has two small verbs for what you do next: keep your head, or grit your teeth and wait it out.
hook.es: Conservó la calma pese a la presión.
hook.en: She kept her calm despite the pressure.

examples.es: Conservó la calma pese a la presión.
examples.en: She kept her calm despite the pressure.
I held out until the end.

examples.es: Tomás perdió la calma cuando llegó la carta.
examples.en: Tomás lost his calm when the letter arrived.
I can't stand this noise any more.
I had to put up with it.

rule:
Two ideas, two verbs.

*Conservar la calma* (or *mantener*, *guardar*) is something you do: you work to stay in control. Its opposite is *perder la calma*. Always keep *la*: *la calma*, never just *calma*.

*Aguantar* is endurance: you take it and do not break. *Aguanté hasta el final* means you lasted. With *no*, it means you have had enough: *No aguanto más*.

*Aguantarse* is to put up with something you cannot change, or bite your tongue: *Me tocó aguantármelo*.

No preposition follows *aguantar*: you stand something, you do not stand "of" it.
smallPrint: Teachers would call *conservar la calma* a verb plus noun collocation, and *aguantarse* a reflexive of resignation.

yourTurn.prompt: Tomás lost his calm. Pick *perdió* or *conservó* and type the whole sentence: *Tomás ___ la calma.*
yourTurn.why: *Perder* means to lose, and *conservar* means to keep, so the meaning picks the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I held out until the end.
yourTurn.why: *Aguanté* is "I" in the past, and it is endurance, so *aguantar* fits.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Please stay calm. (you all)
yourTurn.why: For "you all" the command ends in *-engan*, and *la calma* keeps its *la*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I can't stand this noise any more.
accept: Ya no aguanto más este ruido.
yourTurn.why: *No aguanto* means "I can't stand", and nothing sits between it and the thing.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about yourself: *Conservó la calma pese a la presión.* Say: I kept my calm despite the pressure.
yourTurn.answer: Conservé la calma pese a la presión.
accept: Yo conservé la calma pese a la presión.
yourTurn.why: The ending *-é* says it was me.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it to a friend: stay calm.
yourTurn.why: To one friend the command is short: *mantén*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: She lost her calm in the meeting.
yourTurn.answer: Perdió la calma en la reunión.
accept: Ella perdió la calma en la reunión.
yourTurn.why: *Perdió* is "she lost", and *la calma* is the thing lost.

pitfalls.wrong: Conservé calma pese a la presión.
pitfalls.right: Conservé la calma pese a la presión.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish keeps the article here: *la calma*, where English says just "calm".
Almost. *Aguantar* takes its object directly, with no *de*.
Almost. To last "until" the end you need *hasta*.

personal: Think of the last time something tested you. Say whether you *conservé la calma* or *perdí la calma*, or what you *aguanté*.
